# Eshyra SRD 5.1 — Independent Audit A1

Lane: A1 Owning Bead: `eshyra-o9bd.19.6.7.1` Candidate commit: `6812cc0b89daa0e2503cd06521ec5c60a7103651` Effective review profile: `rules-clause-complete` Review basis: Pinned source archive, generated audit bundle, vendored SRD PDF, repository authority, and captured verification evidence.

## METHOD

### Authority and evidence reviewed

The review uses the accepted authority hierarchy, including `AGENTS.md`, ADR 0017 as narrowed by ADR 0020, the integrated transition design §5.9, `docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md`, `docs/rules-pack-compiler.md`, `docs/importer-fix-protocol.md`, the 68-row finding registry, and the November 1 candidate disclosure.

The audit separates five questions: source fidelity, discovery, semantic adjudication, bounded deterministic execution, and state integrity. A successful test, a typed projection, or a passing gate is not treated as an answer to all five.

The generated pack contains 1,799 records across 16 kinds:

| Kind       | Records |
| ---------- | ------- |
| Action     | 10      |
| Ancestry   | 13      |
| Background | 1       |
| Class      | 12      |
| Condition  | 15      |
| Creature   | 317     |
| Equipment  | 219     |
| Feat       | 1       |
| Feature    | 179     |
| Hazard     | 25      |
| Magic item | 240     |
| Rule       | 325     |
| Spell      | 319     |
| Stat block | 2       |
| Subclass   | 12      |
| Table      | 109     |
| Total      | 1,799   |

The source bundle contains all 403 PDF pages, with per-page text artifacts. The review combines corpus-wide structural checks, targeted mechanical and provenance comparisons, direct examination of source passages and tables, and inspection of the implementation and its producer/consumer paths. These are separate sampling denominators, not a claim that all 1,799 records have been semantically proven against all 403 pages.

### Structural and mechanical probes

The direct artifact checks covered:

- 109/109 table records: 1,077 rows; no row-width mismatches against declared columns. The continuation cases include Bag of Beans on SRD pp. 209–210. Structural integrity does not establish that every cell has the correct meaning.
- 319/319 spells: internal prose-to-projection comparisons for 97 damage-dice projections and 112 saving-throw projections; no mismatches found in those comparisons.
- 317 creature records and 2 inline stat blocks: 514 typed attack-bonus comparisons and 275 saving-throw DC comparisons against their associated text; no discrepancies in those fields. Three of 569 damage-dice text comparisons differed only in Unicode minus-sign representation.
- 103 structured choice groups: inspected option references, cardinality, and repeated option identifiers. No impossible option cardinality or missing referenced option list was detected.
- 240/240 class advancement rows: present with typed advancement data, covering 12 classes and 20 levels each. This is shape and representation evidence, not a proof of correct level-up behavior.
- Relationship declarations: all 29 declaration shapes were examined, including record-key references, condition-name references, and explicit exclusions.

Printed-source checks included the ability-modifier table (p. 76), combat/action prose (pp. 93–94), the condition appendix (pp. 358 onward), and magic-item/table continuations (including pp. 197–198 and 209–210). No corpus-wide negative conclusion follows from those selected page checks.

The captured Vitest result reports 7,377 passed, 3 pending, 0 failed, across 7,380 tests. The suite was not independently executed. Its result is supporting evidence, not independent semantic validation.

### Provenance, discovery, and architecture checks

All 1,799 records carry a `provenance.sourceRef` and page locator. A normalized search found the record name on its cited PDF page in 1,750/1,799 records. The 49 unmatched name anchors comprise 32 tables, 13 rules, 3 equipment records, and 1 magic item. These include generated table titles, normalized section names, and layout-dependent headings; their absence from a simple name search is not itself evidence of invention. It is also not evidence of fidelity.

The relationship census found 655 declared record-key occurrences, 199 declared condition-name occurrences, and 13 explicitly excluded ancestry-source occurrences. A further approximately 1,060 existing-record-key leaves and 433 condition-name leaves were outside those declared shapes. These are disclosure-sensitive discovery gaps, not automatically defects.

The implementation keeps the major responsibilities distinct:

- `discovery/signals.ts`, `candidates.ts`, `expansion.ts`, `retention.ts`, and `packet.ts` implement bounded discovery rather than universal retrieval.
- `rules/recordRelationships.ts` resolves declared relationships using the producing pack's manifest; malformed, unresolved, and excluded outcomes are distinguished rather than silently treated as successful resolution.
- `discovery/packetMessage.ts` identifies source-derived material, projections, relationships, provenance, losses, and capability limits for the DM context.
- `rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts` supplies positive bounded capability bindings rather than inferring execution support from a typed record.
- `orchestrator/orchestrator.ts` defaults discovery to `off`; `shadow` and `intervene` are explicit modes. Therefore, a working offline discovery path is not proof that every live turn receives its context.

The generated gameplay-readiness report explicitly describes itself as non-exhaustive. The magic-item execution-readiness report classifies 1,369 clauses across 240 items: 358 adjudicated by design, 769 engine-pending, 241 green, and 1 design-blocked. These classifications must not be collapsed into claims that all 240 items execute correctly.

The candidate-gates report is also unusually explicit about its limits. Its eight checks all report PASS, but respectively disclaim semantic correctness, upstream PDF authenticity, skipped-test completeness, current registry satisfaction, test discrimination, semantic capability correctness, actual same-seed equivalence, and candidate-document content. Those disclaimers are material to the finding below.

## FINDINGS

### A1-F1 | BLOCKER | Current-candidate discovery disclosure is contradicted by the pinned pack

Invariant and authority. The integrated transition design §5.9, conditions 4 and 9, requires truthful in-band audit/readiness scope and explicit unresolved discovery limits. ADR 0020 requires the pack to distinguish positive, bounded awareness from unbound or unknown support. The rules-pack compiler's source/projection separation applies. A historical document can remain historical, but an artifact presented as current candidate evidence must describe the current candidate accurately.

Evidence at the pinned SHA.

The operative reference chain is:

- `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/README.md:1` identifies `2026-11-01-o9bd-19-6-1-candidate-pack.md` as current candidate evidence.
- `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2026-11-01-o9bd-19-6-1-candidate-pack.md:49–52` states that nested condition-name leaves are outside the current relationship declaration gate, and that one-hop expansion does not continue from an imposing record to its imposed condition record.
- The committed `packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/record-relationships.json` contradicts that general statement. It explicitly declares `/mechanics/conditions/*/condition` as a `record-name` reference for five kinds: `action`, `feat`, `feature`, `hazard`, and `spell`.

A concrete source-backed example is `spell:animal-friendship`. The printed SRD p. 115 says:

> “or be charmed by you for the spell's duration.”

At the pinned commit:

- `records.json`, key `spell:animal-friendship`, contains `data.mechanics.conditions[0] = {"condition":"charmed","relation":"applies"}`.
- `condition:charmed` exists as a separately locatable condition record at SRD p. 358.
- `rules/recordRelationships.ts:resolveRecordRelationships` provides record-name target resolution for this declared pointer.
- `discovery/expansion.ts:expandTypedRelationships` consumes resolved outbound relationships and, for eligible must-consider candidates, adds the target record to the discovery candidates.

The same contradiction can be reproduced as a structural probe by loading `records.json` and `record-relationships.json`, counting the five declarations above, and matching their pointer occurrences to condition names. The pinned data has 191 such top-level condition-name occurrences: 128 spell, 33 feature, 27 hazard, 2 feat, and 1 action. These are not all outside the declaration gate.

This is a source-backed implementation-path observation, not a claim that an independently executed live turn demonstrated the expansion.

The current bundle's `reports/candidate-gates.txt` compounds the currency issue in a bounded way: G-candidate-record PASS observes only that this file exists, with denominator 1, and explicitly says it does not inspect its contents. That gate is truthful about its own observation. The problem is the stale disclosure being presented as current evidence.

Reachability. The discovered condition relationship is available to the staged discovery implementation when the SRD record is selected as a must-consider origin and discovery runs in `intervene` mode. It is not guaranteed on ordinary turns, because `orchestrator.ts` defaults discovery to `off`. The false statement reaches candidate reviewers through the audit README and bundle's candidate-document gate, independently of runtime discovery mode.

Material consequence. The current acceptance evidence misstates the boundary between implemented relationship discovery and undiscovered condition links. A reviewer using this document cannot accurately determine which relationships the candidate already resolves, which it leaves unresolved, or whether new evidence actually closes the previously identified discovery limitation. This violates the bounded truthfulness requirement even though it does not establish a wrong DM ruling or corrupted game state.

Sibling analysis. I searched the 29 relationship declaration shapes and traversed record data for exact existing-record keys and condition names, including undeclared shapes. The defect is not that every condition-name reference has become declared: approximately 433 other condition-name leaves remain undeclared, particularly nested creature mechanics and differently shaped ancestry or magic-item fields. Those remain legitimate disclosed limits. The sibling problem is that the current-candidate document fails to distinguish declared from undeclared subsets after the later implementation changes.

A second currency symptom appears in the same candidate record's downstream-work section: it describes `.19.6.3` as an upcoming gate even though the pinned candidate bundle already contains its generated gate results. Other historical audit documents generally carry explicit historical-scope warnings; I did not promote their old conclusions as separate defects. The remaining-record-key disclosure similarly needs reconciliation with the now-expanded declaration manifest, not a blanket claim that every reference is unresolved.

Owner and proportionate closure. Candidate evidence ownership under `eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4` / formal re-freeze `eshyra-o9bd.14`, with relationship-scope inputs from the existing discovery owners (`eshyra-o9bd.19.3.5` and `eshyra-ry69`).

Preserve the PR #698 document as historical evidence if desired, but stop presenting its unqualified limits as the current candidate's. Provide a pinned-commit disclosure, or an explicit current-candidate amendment, that:

1. Distinguishes condition-name relationships currently declared and resolved from the remaining undeclared families.
2. Describes the one-hop and must-consider expansion limits accurately.
3. Updates the candidate-evidence reference and downstream-stage status without implying universal discovery completeness.

Closure evidence: a reviewed candidate-specific statement cross-checked against the committed relationship manifest and representative record keys, including `spell:animal-friendship` → `condition:charmed`, plus a representative still-undeclared creature condition leaf. The existing relationship resolver and discovery tests can supply behavioral regression evidence; no universal relationship-completeness checker is required.

Recurrence alias: related to the previously disclosed `eshyra-o9bd.19.3.5` and `eshyra-ry69` discovery-limit classes. This finding's distinct class is current-candidate evidence currency, not a new requirement to implement their outstanding references.

Material-change status and required next state: documentary/acceptance-evidence correction; no runtime architectural change is requested. Reconcile the current disclosure, then recheck its candidate identity and affected evidence before accepting the re-freeze. No approval is issued for the pinned candidate while the in-band contradiction remains.

## NO-REQUIREMENT OBSERVATIONS

- Undeclared references do not establish a defect by themselves. A typed key with no relationship declaration cannot be silently counted as discovered, but ADR 0020 does not require every such key to be declared before re-freeze.
- Engine-pending and adjudicated-by-design clauses are not failed deterministic capabilities. The unresolved magic-item backlog is not evidence of a required global executable implementation.
- The freeze guard is currently inactive. The candidate document expressly discloses this and assigns re-enablement to formal re-freeze. It is not a present contradiction of the candidate verification gate.
- `spell:animal-friendship` preserves an apparent printed SRD omission in its higher-level text. Its typed source-defect marker prevents treating an invented correction as licensed source text. The omission is not grounds for an unsourced repair.
- Three Unicode minus-sign differences in creature damage text comparisons are representation differences, not demonstrated damage-mechanics defects.
- G-replay PASS does not prove replay equivalence. The gate expressly says it observes executed evidence pointers, not the semantic strength of their assertions. Its label should not be read more broadly than its in-band scope.

## LIMITS

1. No exhaustive semantic source proof. All 1,799 records were included in structural and provenance scans, but all their prose clauses were not independently checked word-by-word against the 403-page PDF. The selected printed-source comparisons, typed/prose probes, and heading anchors cannot support a claim of zero source-fidelity defects.
2. Forty-nine record names lacked a direct normalized title anchor on the cited PDF pages. The sampled explanations are consistent with normalized headings and generated table titles, but the remaining cases were not individually established as faithful.
3. No independent Node execution. The supplied tests and importer verification were treated as captured evidence. I did not independently rerun Vitest, the compiler, the CLI, or an end-to-end discovery-to-DM-to-state turn.
4. No live DM adjudication experiment. The audit examined context production and execution boundaries, not the consistency of a model's interpretations across actual campaign turns.
5. No complete capability-by-capability runtime proof. The ledger, inventory, readiness report, and representative consumers were examined, but all 115 inventory entries were not independently exercised against adversarial live state. In particular, state persistence, rollback, replay, and multi-turn ownership were not exhaustively tested.
6. No independent live Beads reconciliation. The archive establishes repository authority and the user-supplied A1 assignment; it does not provide a live, authoritative `refs/beads/state` projection suitable for verifying every current dependency and ownership status.
7. No independent upstream-PDF authenticity proof. The supplied PDF, source manifest, pack manifest, and actual bytes agree. That establishes internal identity, not authenticity against a separately obtained upstream publication.

### Audit disposition

The pinned candidate has strong reproducibility evidence, coherent bounded architecture, substantial source-derived representation, and appropriately limited automated gate descriptions. I did not establish a source-fidelity or deterministic state-execution blocker within the examined denominators.

I did establish one acceptance-evidence blocker: the current candidate's linked discovery disclosure no longer agrees with its actual relationship declarations. That is a narrow, correctable truthfulness problem, not a mandate for broader deterministic implementation or complete discovery.

LANE RESULT: BLOCKERS (1)
